chunks: And that which was narrated - Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from an-Nadr from Zur'ah from Muhammad ibn Khalid al-Kazzaz, who said:
I heard Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) saying: 'As for me, I trim from my hair when I intend to depart,' meaning to Mecca for the Ihram.

The meaning is that he trims from his hair that which is other than the head, from his mustache or his body, for there is no harm in trimming that as long as he is not in Ihram. This is indicated by what was narrated:

key_terms.إِحْرَامٌ: The state of consecration for Hajj or Umrah

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on trimming hair before entering Ihram for Hajj?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) clarifies the practical application of the prohibition against cutting hair during Ihram, distinguishing between the hair of the head and other body hair. It establishes that trimming the mustache or body hair is permissible before entering the state of consecration, as the specific restriction applies primarily to the head hair once the pilgrim assumes the sacred state. This ruling highlights the flexibility in personal grooming within the boundaries of ritual purity and consecration.
